content:
maya: quick heads-up — ran int4 conversion for llama2-13b -> mistral-8x (gguf) and hit a tokenizer normalization mismatch with emoji+ZWJ clusters that led to off-by-one token ids and tiny rotary phase drift in the quantized kernel. notes below.

carl: which conversion/quant toolchain? bitsandbytes? ggml packer? gguf exporter version?

maya: convert pipeline = scripts/convert.py + gguf exporter v0.6 + ggml packer v0.9.1 -> int4 fused path. batch=4, seq=1024 for quick bench.

sophie: any minimal repro example we can run locally?

maya: paste pair that repros deterministically on our tokenizer: 

sample text: "Chef\u200d\ud83c\udf55\ud83c\udf73"  (ZWJ cluster: chef + pizza + cook hat)

FP16 token ids: [211, 4201, 55123, 9001]
INT4 token ids:  [211, 4201, 55124, 9001]  <-- 55123 -> 55124 on the ZWJ cluster

from tokenizer checks: 
```
>>> tok.encode("\ud83c\udf55\ud83c\udf73", nfkc=False)
[55123]
>>> tok.encode("\ud83c\udf55\u200d\ud83c\udf73", nfkc=True)
[55124]
```

maya: conversion job accidentally used nfkc=False; original training used nfkc=True. so token id mismatch introduced during save/reload.

ev an: that explains token offsets. but you said there was rotary drift even after fixing ids?

maya: yes — when I forced identical token ids (nfkc normalized on both sides) the logits still diverged by small amounts for tokens in that cluster. suspicion is quant kernel precision + embed_proj ordering interacting with rotary angle rounding.

carl: have we seen similar before? gemma conversion had embed_proj reorder bug last year that produced phase micro-shifts. worth checking embedding projection ordering in the gguf header and the converter.

sophie: please paste a small KV head dump (head 0) fp16 vs int4 so we can inspect phase bytes.

maya: kv dump (first three k vectors head0, float hex):
```
fp16 head0 k[0:3]: [0x3fe0b1c8, 0x3fd23410, 0x3fc990aa]
int4 head0 k[0:3]: [0x3fe0b1c6, 0x3fd23400, 0x3fc99080]
```
notice LSB truncation patterns consistent with quant packer rounding.

ev an: action list to triage: 
1) re-run convert with nfkc=True on both source and target to assert token parity (maya)
2) run deterministic fp16 vs int4 forward with same ids and capture logits + rotary phase diffs (maya + carl)
3) inspect gguf header for embed_proj order & unit test converter roundtrip (sophie)
4) if kernel rounding reproduces, bisect ggml packer and open kernel issue (evan)

maya: started (1) and (2). forcing nfkc=True fixes id parity. (2) still shows ~1e-3 logit drift on those cluster tokens, reproducible across seeds.

carl: reduce the test to seq_len=64 and single batch to isolate rotary wrap. if drift persists at short seq, it's not sequence-length wrap but numeric rounding.

sophie: suggestion: add a post-convert checksum into convert.py that computes sha256 of normalized codepoint sequences for a small probe set (emoji/ZWJ + combining diacritics) and fail the conversion if checksum mismatch. also add a rotary-angle sanity test comparing phase angles on known probe tokens (tolerance threshold).

maya: opening PR with repro and checksum: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2199 — tests/onboard/probes/emoji_zwj_probe.py + converter checksum hook.

infra-bot: Conversion artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-models/conv/1762/llama2-13b->mistral-8x-gguf/conv-1762.tgz. CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/logs/conv-1762

infra-bot: CI triggered for PR #2199: 7 jobs pending.

infra-bot: CI job quant-e2e failed (container OOM/exit 137) during bench step. full logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/jobs/10022

ev an: I'll take the quant-e2e failure and the packer bisect. initial local bisect found rounding at packer commit 3a7b9c introducing LSB shifts. assigning to @evan — will attempt a microfix to preserve low-bit LSBs for rotary-critical dims.

carl: short-term mitigation idea: if probe checksum fails, mark conversion state as review_required and route traffic to fp16 variant for that model. long-term we should aim to make int4 deterministic for these clusters.

sophie: agree. also add an onboarding eval that runs our small emoji probe on every new model conversion and surfaces drift % on the model dashboard.

maya: PR #2199 contains the probe dataset + failing unit test + docs. adding notes about nfkc and why we normalize. will monitor CI and update thread. :thumbsup:

ev an: update EOD — reproduced packer rounding locally and have a candidate patch (preserve sub-byte rounding for first 16 dims). will push to a branch and attach to PR.

maya: thanks. will hold off promoting this conversion until checksum + rotary sanity pass.

infra-bot: job 10022 retriggered by evan on branch evan/packer-fix.

maya: thanks all, keep this thread updated. coffee break for now. :coffee:
